seoTitle: How to Go Live with Your Squarespace Website
metaDescription: Publish your Squarespace site step by step, and find out whether you can go live for free or need to upgrade your plan first.
intro: After you've finished building a Squarespace site, publishing it takes just a few minutes — but you'll need to pick a plan first since Squarespace doesn't offer a free public site. This guide covers logging in, adjusting site availability, and doing a final check before launch.

steps.heading: Log in to Squarespace
steps.body: Sign in to your account, using Continue with Google if that's linked, then land on your dashboard listing all your sites.

steps.heading: Open your site's settings
steps.body: Select the site you want to publish, then go to Settings and click Website to find the options that control public visibility.

steps.heading: Check Site Availability
steps.body: Under Website Settings, find Site Availability. If your site is still private, you'll see an Upgrade to Publish button.

steps.heading: Choose a plan and check out
steps.body: Select the plan that fits your goals, from personal to business tiers, and complete checkout with your payment details.

steps.heading: Do a final review before publishing
steps.body: Check for typos, broken links, or missing images, then confirm the site goes live under your connected domain.

faq.question: Can I publish a Squarespace website for free?
faq.answer: No — Squarespace requires an active paid plan to make a site publicly visible; you'll need to upgrade before it goes live.

faq.question: How long does it take to go live once I upgrade?
faq.answer: Once payment is complete, the site typically goes live immediately.

faq.question: Do I need to connect a domain before publishing?
faq.answer: You can publish without a custom domain first, but connecting one is recommended so visitors can find your site at your chosen web address.

faq.question: What should I check before hitting publish?
faq.answer: Review your site for typos, broken links, and missing images so your first impression is polished.
